summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of chronic pancreatitis, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, bipolar disorder, and alcohol abuse in remission was admitted after passing out in the shower due to severe epigastric pain following a fatty meal. Imaging showed no acute intracranial or abdominal process, with findings consistent with chronic pancreatitis. His pain was managed with IV fluids, bowel rest, and IV analgesics, transitioning to oral oxycodone. An anion gap acidosis was identified and attributed to starvation ketosis, which resolved with dextrose-containing IV fluids. His syncope was deemed consistent with psychogenic nonepileptic events triggered by pain. He tolerated a gradual diet advancement, pain improved, and he was discharged home with medication adjustments, dietary instructions, and follow-up plans with his primary care provider and gastroenterologist.
